messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: canary-eu-west pool reporting elevated errors and latency. 95th latency > 2s, 5xx rate ~12% over last 2m. Impacting ~9% of EU traffic. Paging @devon_oncall and @linda_sre

devon_oncall: ack - taking it. checking dashboards now.

devon_oncall: quick signal: canary weight was accidentally set to 40% in routing rule eu-west/canary instead of 4%. suspecting backend variant mismatch + quant kernel OOMs causing 502s.

linda_sre: pulling logs from canary instances, tailing router and model-runtime. can we reduce canary weight immediately?

devon_oncall: issuing emergency weight flip. running:
```
# emergency flag flip
redwood-ctl routes set-weight --route eu-west --variant canary --weight 0
```

devon_oncall: applied. verifying traffic shift...

carol_ops: noticed immediate drop in 5xx on metrics but latency still elevated on a subset of hosts. some warm caches maybe cold after shift.

linda_sre: running health probes against the previous canary hosts to see if kernel mismatch left them in bad state:
```
curl -sS -D- -o /dev/null http://10.2.14.23:8080/health
# expect 200
```

linda_sre: hosts show repeated segfaults in model-runtime logs referencing quant-kernel.so v1.3.2. tagging for sachin.

sachin_engineering: looking. we recently pushed quant-opt bump 1.3.2 -> 1.3.3 to canary only. if that's the case, we should roll the canary variant binary back to 1.3.1 and re-run warmup.

devon_oncall: agree. taking two-step: 1) maintain canary weight 0, 2) start rollback of model binary on canary hosts, 3) throttle new requests to warm caches. Executing rollback via rollout job.

devon_oncall: rollback job kicked off: job id rj-2026-09-15-42. ETA ~6m to replace binaries and warm kv caches.

eva_support: heads up - support triage is preparing an update for affected customers. initial ETA message: "We've mitigated elevated errors for EU customers; engineering investigating root cause. We will update within 30 minutes." please confirm.

carol_ops: confirmed visible error-rate back to baseline for most routes. small tail of errors (~0.3%) persist for customers tied to sticky sessions on the old canary hosts.

linda_sre: parity check after rollback: 1) model-runtime stable, 2) no segfaults in logs, 3) 95th latency back under 600ms. Monitoring for 10 minutes.

devon_oncall: creating incident ticket and handoff. Incident summary: "Regional rollout misconfiguration (canary weight) + canary-only quant kernel bump caused runtime segfaults -> increased 5xx for ~9% EU traffic. Mitigations: emergency canary weight flip to 0, rollback quant kernel to stable binary, warmed caches, throttled traffic. Customer impact limited and recovered after mitigation." Linking runbook: https://runbooks.internal/rb/canary-rollout-emergency

devon_oncall: paging next oncall for continuity: handing to @linda_sre. I will stay on until support update published.

linda_sre: ack, taking over monitoring and postmortem lead. I'll coordinate with sachin for root-cause analysis and schedule a blameless postmortem.

sachin_engineering: we have a repro locally of the segfault with 1.3.2 quant build. will push hotfix and a test to the CI gate to prevent canary-only kernel bumps without integration testing.

eva_support: publishing customer update now. ETA ~3m.

carol_ops: note for follow-up runbook changes: add a pre-rollout rule to verify canary weight is <= 10% and add a canary-traffic-alert alarm to automute weights on >5xx threshold.

linda_sre: handing off to oncall rotation at +2h. current state: stable, no new 5xx, metrics normal. I'll file the incident and assign action items.

devon_oncall: thanks team. final note: PD incident created INC-20260915-87. timeline saved. :white_check_mark:

linda_sre: closing slack thread for handoff; will update with postmortem link when available.
